content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Both queues are understaffed because of absence, not extra demand. Payments has 54 agents against 66.2 expected; general has 51 against 61.4. Attendance shows 15 absences in payments and 13 in general, against usual daily levels of about 2.8 and 2.6. Most are agents who 'went home unwell after lunch' (12 in payments, 10 in general), plus 3 sick calls in each queue. Demand does not explain the shortfall. General volume is about 23% below forecast in recent intervals. Payments is only about 5% above forecast for the day, with a modest rise in card_declined calls. There is no matching incident (only a branch-printer P4) and no marketing entry. Despite the reduced staff, service level has been 100% with zero abandons in every interval since 16:45 on both queues.","plan_name":"Monitor only – no further spend for the evening","rationale":"Service level is already well above the 80/20 target on both queues with the current reduced headcount. Volumes are tapering toward close at 20:00, and general is running well under forecast. Further overtime would cost Rs 360 per accepted agent-hour for little benefit. Callbacks or deflection would add customer friction with no service gain. Cross-skill moves and break delays are not needed. The overtime offers made at 13:45 end at 18:15. The supervisor should still watch payments, because its 18:00 interval came in 22% over forecast with only 32 agents on phones. If payments service level drops below about 85%, the first response should be to move a few general agents to payments, which is free while general holds at 100%.","actions":[]}
